onboarding.title: Set up Nox
onboarding.welcomeText: Nox is your local AI assistant. Let's set it up in a few steps.
onboarding.depsInstallDesc: Nox needs additional AI libraries (PyTorch, EasyOCR, Sentence-Transformers). These are downloaded once.
onboarding.depsSkipHint: Skipping is possible, but AI features won't be available until installed.
onboarding.ollamaHint: Please install and start Ollama (ollama serve), then continue.
onboarding.backendSelectHint: Choose which AI engine Nox should use:
onboarding.backendOllamaDesc: Local AI engine – easy to install, many models available.
onboarding.backendOtherDesc: Use an external OpenAI-compatible server of your choice.
onboarding.backendNoxDesc: Built-in AI engine (llama.cpp) – no external software needed. Experimental.
onboarding.otherCustomHint: Enter the URL of your OpenAI-compatible server.
onboarding.otherProviderHint: Start the server in your software and select it here. Nox connects automatically.
onboarding.providerLMStudioDesc: Popular desktop app for local LLMs
onboarding.providerOllamaCompatDesc: Another Ollama server on the network
onboarding.lmStudioHint: Start LM Studio and enable the local server. Nox connects automatically.
onboarding.noxExperimentalHint: The built-in engine loads GGUF models directly in the Nox process. No external software needed. Note: This feature is still experimental and may contain bugs.
onboarding.modelHintLmStudio: Download a model in your server and activate it. Nox uses the currently active model.
onboarding.modelHintNox: Select a GGUF model in the settings. You can skip this step and configure it later.
onboarding.voiceHint: Choose your language and a voice for Nox. The system language was detected automatically.
onboarding.wakeWordLangWarning: The wake word "Hey Nox" is optimized for German. In other languages it is active but likely won't work reliably.
onboarding.modelHint: Select the Ollama model Nox should use.
onboarding.noModels: No models found. Please pull a model:
onboarding.micTestHint: Select which audio devices Nox should use.
onboarding.micTestNote: You can use Nox via voice or text.
onboarding.micSkip: Text chat is still fully usable. Voice will be disabled.
onboarding.audioDevicesHint: Select which microphone and speakers Nox should use.
onboarding.noAudioDevices: No audio devices found. You can use Nox via text.
onboarding.wakeHint: Say 'Hey Nox' 3 times to test detection.
onboarding.wakeModelHint: The wake word model is built-in. You can skip this step and use Nox via text or mic button.
onboarding.setupCompleteText: Nox is ready. You can now ask questions, use voice, and capture context.
onboarding.analyticsOptIn: Allow anonymous usage analytics (helps improve Nox, no content/IPs)
onboarding.gpuCpuFallback: CUDA not available – Nox runs in CPU mode. Voice will be slower, text chat works normally.
onboarding.downloadComplete: Download complete! Wake word model is ready.
onboarding.wakeWordBuiltin: Wake word model is built-in (Hey Nox). You can test calibration in the next step.
onboarding.recommendedModelDesc: Qwen 3 14B – best balance of quality, tool-calling and speed for Nox.
onboarding.wakeWordLangWarningHelp: Help us improve: Send your voice recordings via a ticket on our Discord server to train the wake word for your language.
onboarding.speedModeSelected: Speed mode selected — applies to generation parameters.
